text.p: MobileMedia Corp said it did not make a scheduled $5.6 million interest payment due under its credit agreement in an effort to conserve cash, and while it is continuing efforts to modify payment terms, it may seek Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection should talks with creditors fail to result in agreeable terms.
The company had announced last week that it did not make interest payments on its 9-3/8 percent senior subordinated debt due 2007, for the same reason.
MobileMedia said it is also seeking to modify payment terms with certain of its largest vendors, some of which have not been paid at scheduled dates.

It said Motorola Inc has said it will require credit support to assure payment of $34 million in past due accounts payable, and will suspend all shipments until the companies have been able to reach an agreement.

MobileMedia said its bank lenders have been supportive of efforts to reach an agreement with Motorola, and have indicated that the issuance of letters of credit to support the obligation to Motorola would be issued.

The company said the failure to make these scheduled interest payments is an event of default under its credit deal. These events of default permit the banks to exercise various remedies, including acceleration of relevant debt obligations.

It said its advisers are in discussions with the bank lenders regarding this default, but said that in the event of a Chapter 11 filing, it would enter into a debtor-in-possession credit agreement that would provide it with sufficient working capital to sustain business operations.
